text:
sam: Getting repeated P1s this morning for noisy 'High error rate' alerts on api.requests.count for two customers (ACME, BetaCorp). Dashboards look steady but alerts started at 09:02 UTC.

maria: which alert rule / id?

sam: rule id alerts/rr-5xx-rate-v2 — threshold is 5% over 1m. Multiple fires across regions. Logs show no 5xx spike.

jess: could be an aggregation/rollup artefact. If minute buckets get zeros or are shifted because of late ingestion, relative-change rules can spike.

tao: I pulled raw metric series for ACME 08:55-09:10 UTC and compared to per-minute rollups. Raw shows continuous request flow and normal 5xx rate ~0.2%. Rollup emits a 0 value at 09:01 then normal at 09:02; percent-change computation sees a jump from 0 -> normal and flags it.

maria: can you get rollup worker logs around 08:58-09:05? `kubectl logs -l app=metrics-rollup -n prod --since=20m` should show warnings if backpressure.

sam: pasted relevant log lines:
```
[08:59:58] warn shard-7: window_end missing for 2023-07-21T09:00:00Z
[09:00:02] info backlog=11350
[09:01:07] info processed backlog=11350, emitting aggregated buckets
```

jess: backlog + late emit = some minute buckets aggregated with many delayed events while the immediate bucket got nothing -> spurious zeros and jumps. Percent-change alerts are vulnerable.

tao: root cause looks like ingest-proxy having a GC/network hiccup -> retry flood into Kafka. Rollup currently buckets by ingestion_time, so delayed messages are placed into the later minute.

maria: immediate mitigation: mute relative-change alerts when baseline sample count < 10 and add a rule-level guard to ignore antecedent=0. For the incident I've muted rr-5xx-rate-v2 for the affected customer labels and created a suppression window.

support-bot: Incident INC-2023-7894 created and assigned to eng-sre + metrics team. Severity P2.

sam: suppression applied for ACME/BetaCorp via console override. Alerts stopped firing.

jess: medium-term fix: change rollup to bucket on event_time with a configurable lateness window (30s), mark late-emitted buckets and do not treat missing buckets as zero when comparing relative change, and emit a metric `rollup.lateness_seconds`.

tao: opened PR #482 in metrics-rollup: event_time bucketing + backlog backpressure; also adding unit tests that replay out-of-order messages.

maria: ops follow-ups: add alerts for `rollup.backlog_size > 1000` and `rollup.lateness_seconds > 30`, and add runbook steps to pause percent-change alerts and switch to absolute thresholds when rollup lateness is high.

jess: repro plan for validation after PR: 1) simulate ingest pause for 2m, 2) send 12k events with event_time skewed, 3) resume ingest, 4) confirm per-minute rollups have no zero-gap artifacts and alerts remain quiet.

tao: repro commands I used locally:
```
# scale ingest down
kubectl scale deploy ingest-proxy --replicas=0 -n prod
# generate delayed events with event_time offset -90s
python loadgen.py --count 12000 --event_time_offset=-90
# scale ingest back up
kubectl scale deploy ingest-proxy --replicas=3 -n prod
```
Then watch metrics-rollup logs and the alert stream.

maria: timeline: suppression applied 09:10, backlog drained 09:12, PR opened 11:05. Keeping thread open until PR merges and staging validation completes.

sam: please add the repro steps + suppression TTL to the customer incident notes. I left a short note but expand please.

jess: adding notes to INC-2023-7894 and pinging @ops to onboard rollup metrics to dashboards.

alerts-bot: Muted rule `rr-5xx-rate-v2` for labels {customer:ACME,BetaCorp} until 2023-07-21T09:40:00Z by maria.

maria: leaving the thread open. If anyone sees similar spikes, DM me. :eyes:
